Through a process of reflection and catharsis the sculptures were created in carefully devised, movement informed workshops with individuals who have experience of grief. Produced and performed in private, the enigmatic forms are instinctual. Appearing as remnants of ancient ritual or mark-making used to inscribe territory, scent o In this work notions of rotation and renewal are threaded into queered perspectives on grief, temporality and natural processes. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Metropolitan University has been allocated £16 million from the Greater Manchester Good Growth Fund to establish FUSE-M, a groundbreaking innovation facility bringing together immersive technologies, AI and advanced manufacturing to help businesses develop, test and co The allocation forms a key part of the latest round of investment from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which has earmarked funding for a range of projects through the innovation strand of its Good Growth Fund FUSE-M (Future User-centred Simulation, Enterprise and Manufacturing) will be a 1,600 sq m business-facing innovation facility located in Hulme, where organisations can explore, test and adopt emerging technologies The project brings together manufacturing expertise from Manchester Met’s award winning advanced additive manufacturing facility PrintCity, and Centre for Digital Modelling and Analysis for Cultural Heritage (D-MACH) facility, alongside creative and digital expertise from the Uni The new facility will be a specialist innovation space providing companies with access to advanced simulation, digital modelling, immersive technologies, digital twins, prototyping and manufacturing capabilities The facility has already attracted support from major industry partners including Siemens, HP, Matsuura, TEKEVER and The Vita Group and will work alongside key regional innovation assets including Atom Valley, Manchester Science Park and the Henry Royce Institute

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Funding is set to double to support a pledge by the prime minister to give every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas Ending rough sleeping was one of Andy Burnham's first promises when he entered Downing Street, announcing a £442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support Ahead of the first Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street on Monday, No 10 has indicated a further £432m will be added to the initiative in Wednesday's Budget Shadow housing secretary Katie Lam said rough sleeping had hit "record highs under Labour" and criticised Burnham for failing to end rough sleeping when he was the Mayor of Greater Manchester The BBC understands the government's commitment is that every rough sleeper will be able to physically move into accommodation by Christmas and/or they will be offered support as a way to prevent them sleeping rough Some people may choose not to accept accommodation, but ministers say support will still be offered to them

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where a Sex Pistols show that inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas" He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk" As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). Manchester-based Crediflow AI automates the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. The company has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts – a process the industry calls financial spreading – analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. They labelled them a ‘backwards step’ for and an ‘unwelcome curtailing’ of democra Under the new rules planning applications would be split into two tiers – Schedule 1 applications and Schedule 2 applications, designated by planning officers. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers Schedule 2 covers larger applications, which may be brought before the planning committee, if agreed by the planning committee chair and the council’s chief planning officer. The move also removes elected members’ right to ‘call in’ a planning application for scrutiny and debate The new rules came into force at the end of October, with Bury council now having approved the change in its constitution needed to meet the new legal requirements. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside LIVE Updated 4 mins ago Droylsden explosives arrests LIVE as residents evacuated after bomb squad response Police said 'ammunition and potentially hazardous substances' were uncovered at a house in Droylsden The police scene in place in Droyl A major emergency services response descended on Shelley Grove in Droylsden on Wednesday afternoon (November 18), with police, fire and ambulance crews all in attendance. Bomb disposal experts were also called to the scene following the discovery at the property A cordon was put in place and residents were evacuated from their homes. Greater Manchester Police said officers attended the address at 2.22pm to make an arrest attempt as part of an ongoing and unrelated investigation A force spokesperson said: "Emergency services attended the scene, and officers recovered ammunition and discovered potentially hazardous substances. There is a cordon in place while the EOD (Explosive Ordnance Disposal) assesses the situation." Officers said a man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of criminal damage, arson, and possession of ammunition. A man in his 70s and a woman in her 60s have been arrested on suspicion of unlawfully possessing ammunition and explosive substances, GMP said In a post on the GMP Tameside Facebook page last night, police said the evacuation of the street was likely to remain in place today (Thursday). "As a precaution, residents on the affected street have been evacuated while emergency services continue their work", the post said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Gang used cruel cash machine trick to steal thousands from pensioners The three men would work together to distract their 'vulnerable' targets Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:49, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Three members of an organised crime gang have been jailed after they stole thousands of pounds from pensioners across the country using a cruel trick at cash machines Ionut Matei, 40, Vasile Ciubotaru, 45, and Ramonel Mandache, 51, together stole more than £40,000 from their 'vulnerable' victims. The trio targeted people using ATMs in Halifax bank, including in the Stockport and Bury branches, and at Lloyds Bank Detectives found Matei, Ciubotaru and Mandache, who are all Romanian nationals, would travel across the country during their malicious enterprise. To trick their victims, one of the men would stand close enough to see them entering their pin into the cash machine Another would distract them by drawing attention to a banknote deliberately placed on the floor nearby, Cheshire Police said. The third man would then swipe their bank card and replace it with a similar-looking card Victims were left completely unaware that their card had been stolen. The gang would then use the stolen cards and PIN to withdraw cash and buy items, often before the victims had realised what had happened

The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamorous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

Greater Manchester Police raised public safety concerns following two recent incidents outside the venue CCTV footage played at the hearing showed an incident on Saturday, November 7 just after 2am. A group of people appeared to be gathered outside the pub after closing time PC Stuart Hammersley said: "Up to 15 people [were] involved in large-scale disorder. We saw punches, kicks, people thrown to the floor... andthis continued on for about eight minutes "One of the victims was taken to hospital with a suspected fractured eye socket. A Section 20 wounding crime has been recorded and is still being investigated."

Emergency services raced out to Holmes Chapel station at around 7.30pm on Tuesday evening (October 27) British Transport Police says it was called out to reports of a passenger suffering a medical emergency. The man, aged in his late 20s, was sadly pronounced dead at the scene The incident is not thought to be suspicious. A British Transport Police spokesperson said: "We were called to Holmes Chapel station at around 7.30pm on Tuesday, October 27 following reports of a passenger suffering a medical emergency on a train "Officers attended along with paramedics but despite their efforts sadly the person was pronounced dead at the scene. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Money Manchester firm that took £123,000 from struggling businesses shut down The firm wrongly told companies that they could avoid reputational damage by selling their companies before liquidation - while charging fees of up to £6,800 Add to preferre A Manchester firm that took £123,000 from 51 struggling businesses was shut down by the High Court on Thursday (October 29). Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of companies with debts by providing 'misleading services', the government's Insolvency Service has said The Manchester-registered company was found to be offering 'alternatives' to formal insolvency to directors of the companies in financial difficulty. It offered to arrange sales of 'financially distressed' businesses for £1 whilst charging fees of between £2,500 and £6,800 It comes following an Insolvency Service investigation which has subsequently led to the firm being shut down Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, David Usher, said: "Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of struggling businesses by offering directors a misleading route out of their company’s debts, charging thousands of pounds for the service "Selling a company does not prevent its former directors’ conduct from being investigated if it later enters liquidation

The 35-year-old man suffered a cardiac arrest close to the end of the 13.1-mile race near Lancashire Cricket Club's ground in Old Final-year medical student Megan McGillin was providing first aid cover at the event when she saw the man collapse. The University of Manchester , where Megan is studying, said he fell to the ground as he crossed through the finish line The university said she recognised 'the signs of cardiac arrest within seconds' then raised the alarm and began life-saving chest compressions while calling for additional help As a wider medical team arrived, Megan is said to have continued working calmly under pressure. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Michelle Pearson 'was trying the best for her family' before horrific Walkden arson attack killed five Salford Council received an anonymous tip-off that the children were in “great danger” days before they were murdered, but this was not pass A mother-of-six who was killed in an arson attack on her Salford home was trying the best for her family "right until the end", an inquest into her death has heard Michelle Pearson and her four youngest children - Demi Pearson, 14, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three - were also murdered as flames engulfed the house, on Jackson Street, Walkden , in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their killer, Zak Bolland, was involved in a feud with one of the 37-year-old's older sons, and was later jailed for life with an accomplice for the murders. Ms Pearson had called police multiple times and asked to be rehoused before suffering fatal injuries in the firebombing of She told police she did not feel safe after receiving firebombing threats on her property, having her windows smashed, her bin set on fire and graffiti daubed on walls of her home Tributes to Michelle Pearson and her children outside their Walkden home (Image: M.E.N.)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS More strikes expected at four Greater Manchester hospitals after staff reject pay offer Nearly all theatre staff voted to reject the Northern Care Alliance's offer Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Write More strikes are expected at a crisis-hit NHS trust after hundreds of theatre staff overwhelmingly rejected its latest offer in a long-running dispute over overtime pay Nearly all (99 per cent) of more than 400 theatre staff, including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers, working across four hospitals voted to reject the Northern Care Alliance's (NCA) offer The Trust, which runs Salford Royal, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield General Hospital in Bury , said it was "very disappointing" that workers had rejected what it described as its "best offer" to end the dispute Trade union Unison, which represents the striking workers, said staff had sent a "resounding message" to NCA bosses and confirmed staff would continue to strike The dispute centres on the use of an outside agency called NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage additional shifts, with Unison claiming the arrangements could leave some workers earning up to £80 less per shift than under previous arrangements

The rail firmed announced that around 70 additional Sunday services will return this winter following its landmark agreement with the RMT union, which comes ahead of a new timetable next The agreement between Northern and the RMT union brought to an end the the longest-running industrial dispute on the railway and paved the way for a phased return of Sunday services across the North West. Around 70 additional trains are expected to return each Sunday this winter, The additional services will be introduced over the coming weeks, with priority given to routes which have had little or no Sunday train service for more than two years, as well as supporting major events such as the region's Christmas markets. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Police descend on Salford flat block with woman 'critical' in hospital Officers were called to the scene at Malus Court in Pendleton on Sunday afternoon Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 10:13, 26 Oct A woman was rushed to hospital in a critical condition after emergency crews were called to a flat block in Salford Police and paramedics descended on the scene at Malus Court, on Belvedere Road in the Pendleton area, at around 2.40pm on Sunday (October 25). Crews responded to reports of a 'concern for the welfare of a woman' The woman was rushed to hospital by paramedics. She remains there in a critical condition, a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said Amid the incident, two men, aged 54 and 58, were arrested. They were both arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs. The 54-year-old man was further arrested on suspicion of racially/religiously aggravated harassment GMP has not revealed any further information on the incident. Residents reported seeing a large police presence in the area on Sunday afternoon, with a police car reportedly remaining on the scene overnight and into this morning (Monday)

The two groups were kept apart by metal fences manned by dozens of police officers Both events passed off without serious incident although the Manchester Evening News witnessed one man being escorted away by police. Greater Manchester Police responded to reports of a vehicle being stolen on Wilson Street in Swinton, Salford, at aroun The car was later spotted on the M60 by the National Police Air Service, the police helicopter. It was then pursued on the M60 before moving on the M62. The pursuit ended in west Yorkshire, on the eastbound carriageway of the M62 between junction 26, near Cleckheaton, and junctio The crash involved the suspected stolen vehicle and police tactical unit cars, the force said. A member of the public was taken to hospital with non-life-changing injuries. Part of the motorway between junctions 26 and 27 was shut for a time after the collision National Highways said the closure was in place 'due to a multi-vehicle collision'. A GMP spokesman said: "The driver failed to stop for officers, prompting a pursuit which continued onto the M62, with assistance from West Yorkshire Police "Between junctions 26 and 27 of the M62, the vehicle collided with GMP tactical aid unit vehicles, causing damage to the police vehicles."

A police chase ensued, and the stolen car lost control before veering onto a grass verge and smashing into a parked vehicle A white British man, aged 41, was arrested at the scene on suspicion of a burglary and serious assault. That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes.
